item.text:
**3B.7 Research Note: Abiy Ahmed in 2024**

Overall: **mixed but leaning strongly negative**. I found several government/UN partnership efforts aimed at displacement, refugee support, and girls/women’s services, but the year was dominated by evidence of civilians, refugees, and minorities being exposed to targeted violence, mass displacement, arbitrary detention, and abuse with little sign of effective state protection.

- **Second Phase of PROSPECTS Launched in Ethiopia, Empowering Refugees, IDPs and Host Communities** | UNICEF Ethiopia | 2024-03-21 | https://www.unicef.org/ethiopia/press-releases/second-phase-prospects-launched-ethiopia-empowering-refugees-idps-and-host  
  Ethiopia, the Netherlands, and UN agencies launched a partnership to strengthen resilience, self-reliance, and inclusion for refugees, IDPs, and host communities through education, livelihoods, protection, and infrastructure. This is positive but programmatic evidence, not proof that violence against vulnerable groups was actually prevented.  
  QIDs: `3B.7`  
  Also informs: `3B.4`, `3B.6`

- **UN agencies and Ethiopian government launch Durable Solutions Strategy for internal displacement** | UN Ethiopia / UNHCR | 2024-11-11 | https://ethiopia.un.org/en/283776-ethiopia-launches-national-strategy-implement-solutions-pathways-internal-displacement  
  The government and UN launched a national strategy to shift from emergency relief toward durable solutions for IDPs, including voluntary return, local integration, reintegration, coordination, and accountability. This is the strongest positive institutional evidence, but it remains a strategy launch, not demonstrated protection outcomes.  
  QIDs: `3B.7`  
  Also informs: `3B.4`, `3B.6`, `2B.7`

- **UN Women, Partners deliver training on Gender-Responsive Reintegration Service to Migrant Women Returnees** | United Nations in Ethiopia | 2024-07-26 | https://ethiopia.un.org/en/277273-un-women-partners-deliver-training-gender-responsive-reintegration-service-migrant-women  
  UN Women and the Ministry of Women and Social Affairs trained government stakeholders on safe and dignified reintegration services for migrant women returnees. This is a real protection-oriented step for a vulnerable group, but it is limited in scope and not evidence of broad protection from targeted violence.  
  QIDs: `3B.7`  
  Also informs: `3B.4`, `3B.6`

- **UNHCR Ethiopia | Country Refugee Response Plan | January–December 2024** | UNHCR | 2024-04-30 | https://data.unhcr.org/en/documents/details/108335  
  The plan was co-led by the Ethiopian Refugees and Returnees Service and UNHCR and set out coordination and financing for refugee needs and host communities. This supports a limited positive reading of state coordination, but not proof of effective civilian protection on the ground.  
  QIDs: `3B.7`  
  Also informs: `3B.4`, `3B.6`

- **Ethiopia: Military Executes Dozens in Amhara Region** | Human Rights Watch | 2024-04-04 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/04/04/ethiopia-military-executes-dozens-amhara-region  
  HRW reported Ethiopian forces summarily killed dozens of civilians in Merawi and committed other war crimes in Amhara. This is strong evidence that the government did not protect civilians from targeted state violence in 2024.  
  QIDs: `3B.7`  
  Also informs: `3B.1`, `3B.2`, `2B.9`

- **Ethiopia: Merawi killings should be independently investigated** | Amnesty International | 2024-04-12 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/04/ethiopia-merawi-killings-should-be-independently-investigated/  
  Amnesty said ENDF soldiers rounded up local men in Merawi and shot and killed scores after fighting with Fano, and it criticized the lack of credible government efforts to ensure justice. This is direct evidence of failure to shield vulnerable civilians from massacre and to provide follow-up protection.  
  QIDs: `3B.7`  
  Also informs: `3B.1`, `3B.2`, `2B.9`

- **Ethiopia: Fighting, Abuses Putting Sudanese Refugees at Risk** | Human Rights Watch | 2024-10-17 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/10/17/ethiopia-fighting-abuses-putting-sudanese-refugees-risk  
  HRW said fighting in Amhara put Sudanese refugees in camps at grave risk and that they faced killings, beatings, looting, forced labor, and unsafe relocation pressure. That is strong evidence of failure to protect a highly vulnerable displaced population.  
  QIDs: `3B.7`  
  Also informs: `3B.1`, `3B.2`, `3B.5`

- **World Report 2025: Ethiopia** | Human Rights Watch | 2025-01-16 | https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2025/country-chapters/ethiopia  
  HRW’s retrospective on 2024 says government forces in Amhara carried out extrajudicial executions, sexual violence, torture, and ill-treatment against civilians, while Sudanese refugees in camps were subjected to attacks and abuses. This is strong corroboration that women, children, refugees, and other vulnerable groups were not adequately protected in 2024.  
  QIDs: `3B.7`  
  Also informs: `3B.1`, `3B.2`, `2B.9`

**Assessment**

- The positive evidence is real but narrow: it is mostly **program design, coordination, and training** for IDPs, refugees, and migrant women returnees.
- The negative evidence is much stronger: **massacres, sexual violence, refugee abuse, and conflict-driven displacement** show that vulnerable groups were not reliably protected.
- Search gap: I did **not** find strong 2024 evidence that Abiy’s government successfully protected minorities or vulnerable groups from targeted violence at scale. The available positive material is mostly planning and partner-led programming, not demonstrated protection outcomes.
